known.title: Preserve Windows coverage for shared fixtures inside test modules
Retain coverage for pytest_plugins fixture consumers

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - tests share fixtures through pytest_plugins.
The dependency graph handles only Import and ImportFrom nodes, so pytest_plugins registrations create no dependency edge. This mechanism is already used in tests/test_one_company.py:8, which registers test_python_starter and consumes its fixture at line 35. Those consumers remain absent from the picker's expanded selection. When a shared test module has only plugin consumers and no platform marker itself, the CI classifier also incorrectly emits test-only=true and run-windows=false, skipping affected Windows tests. This is new evidence beyond the settled standard-import case. Account for pytest_plugins dependencies in the shared graph and its generated copy so shared modules retain their consumers and platform coverage.
findings.title: Retain coverage for pytest_plugins fixture consumers

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round with a simpler rule: a changed test file counts as shared when any other test file names it, so imports, pytest_plugins and other links all keep their users

why: A pull request that changes only one test file runs all six Linux test groups and all five Windows groups, about 30 minutes of checks for one test
